help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Although he knew the risks, he signed the contract.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The study has methodological flaws; nevertheless it provides valuable pointers.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: The verb follows directly, so position 1 needs an adverb: gleichwohl. wiewohl, obgleich and zumal are subordinators and would send the verb to the end.
help.tips[0].en.text: Subordinators send the verb to the end: wiewohl, obschon, obgleich, obzwar, zumal, insofern als. Adverbs take position 1 (verb second) or sit in the middle field: indes, indessen, gleichwohl, nichtsdestoweniger, dessen ungeachtet, mithin, somit, folglich. Coordinators stand outside the clause (position 0) and change nothing: aber, doch, allein.
help.tips[0].en.title: Three word-order classes
help.tips[0].en.trap: gleichwohl is not a subordinator in standard German: “…, gleichwohl sie wertvolle Hinweise liefert” is marked as wrong.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The minister promised swift help; those affected, however, are still waiting for it.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The guests were chatting in the drawing room. Meanwhile the host was preparing dessert in the kitchen.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Two actions run side by side with no contrast, and indessen opens the clause in position 1: the temporal reading, ‘meanwhile’.
help.tips[1].en.text: Adversative “however” (= jedoch), usually in the middle field: Die Betroffenen warten indes bis heute darauf. Temporal “meanwhile” (= währenddessen, unterdessen), usually in position 1: Indessen bereitete der Gastgeber das Dessert vor. The context decides which reading is meant.
help.tips[1].en.title: indes / indessen: two meanings
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: We should accept the offer, especially as the terms are unlikely to get any better.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The cancellation is surprising, all the more since the club had only confirmed its participation in May.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: zumal is subordinating, so the finite verb goes to the end of its clause.
help.tips[2].en.text: zumal (da / weil) adds a further, decisive reason to something already stated: “especially as, all the more since”. It is subordinating, so the verb goes to the end, and the zumal-clause normally follows the main clause.
help.tips[2].en.title: zumal: the reason that tips the balance
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: The accused was abroad at the time of the offence; consequently he cannot have committed it.
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: He wanted to help, but he lacked the means.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The second clause is the logical conclusion of the first, so it takes mithin (‘consequently’), an adverb that sits in the middle field.
help.tips[3].en.text: mithin (formal “consequently”) draws a logical conclusion, like somit and folglich. insofern als / insoweit als restrict a claim (“in so far as”); the two halves can also be split: nur insoweit bindend, als … . allein at the head of a clause is an elevated “but” and does not invert. respektive (bzw.) links items that correspond one to one.
help.tips[3].en.title: mithin, insofern als, allein, respektive
help.context.en: The commission submitted its report on time; the government, however, is hesitating to implement it. Although the findings are clear, it intends to wait for further expert opinions first – especially as elections are due in the autumn. The opposition considers this tactically motivated; nevertheless it too concedes that some recommendations would be expensive. The report is therefore not only a technical but also a political document. Everyone wants to act, but there is disagreement about how.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: gleichwohl is an adverb in standard German: it triggers verb-second order, not verb-final.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: zumal is a subordinator: the finite verb goes to the end.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: As a conjunction, allein stands in position 0 like aber; the clause keeps its normal order.
help.hookEn: Indes, wiewohl, zumal, mithin: the elevated connectors of serious prose — and the word order each one demands.
help.introEn: These elevated connectors are rarely new in meaning — most of them have an everyday twin you already know (aber, obwohl, weil, trotzdem, deshalb) — but they differ in register, in the exact logical relation they express and, crucially, in the word order they trigger. This quiz drills 18 sentences: indes / indessen as adversative “however” and as temporal “meanwhile”; wiewohl, obschon, obgleich and wenn auch as elevated concessive connectors; zumal (da) for “especially as”; gleichwohl, nichtsdestoweniger and dessen ungeachtet as concessive adverbs with verb-second order; mithin and somit for a logical conclusion; insofern als and the split insoweit …, als for restriction; allein as literary “but” outside the clause; and respektive. Every cue gives the English meaning and the word-order slot you must fill, and every synonym that fits both is accepted.
help.rememberEn[0]: Subordinators (wiewohl, obschon, zumal, insofern als) → verb at the end.
help.rememberEn[1]: Adverbs (indes, gleichwohl, dessen ungeachtet, mithin) → verb second or in the middle field.
help.rememberEn[2]: allein = aber in position 0: no inversion.
help.rememberEn[3]: indes can mean “however” or “meanwhile” — read the context.
sentences[4].whyEn: wenn auch … so doch — the adjectival concession.
